page: Microsoft Azure M64-32ms is a memory-intensive server instance powered by the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features an Intel Xeon 8280L processor with an x86_64 architecture, providing 16 physical cores and 32 dedicated vCPUs running at 2.7 GHz. The hardware configuration includes a massive 1792.0 GB of system memory, yielding 56.0 GB of RAM per core. Local storage is provided via a 2097 GB SSD, and the instance is Premium Storage capable. No GPUs are included in this configuration.

Benchmark data indicates a clear performance profile. Single-core CPU performance is positioned in the bottom 10% across stress-ng, Geekbench, and single-threaded compression tests. However, multi-core CPU performance and memory bandwidth consistently rank in the middle 50% average tier. Database operations, Redis SET operations achieving 20.7 million operations per second, and static web serving throughput at 17.08 GB/sec also fall within the average tier. Large-model LLM inference is a notable bottleneck, with prompt processing for a 70B model scoring in the bottom 10% and text generation for smaller models ranking in the bottom 25%.

Given the massive memory allocation relative to the compute resources, this instance offers high resource density for memory-bound workloads rather than compute-heavy tasks. The qualitative cost profile reflects a specialized hardware class where the primary value lies in hosting large in-memory datasets. The server is highly suited for large-scale databases, in-memory caching systems like Redis, and enterprise applications requiring extensive memory footprints, while it is less optimal for single-threaded processing or intensive AI inference workloads.
